questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To get transfered courses which were hard in copenhagen, as would be easier to take in Barcelona.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked my visit to Barcelona. I got some new international friends, and some new friends from Denmark, which I will meet when I get home to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite hard. Especially to find an apartment. But I found out when I was arrived to Barcelona, that I could have asked for accomodation via the University, so that was a missed opportunity to make the practical stof easier done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much but it was easy to communicate with the office international. But most stuff I had to figure out myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Was hard to find courses that was not overlapping. Hard to figure out what the specific recuraments and minimum grade was needed to pass the courses.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Dont use Live-It, a company who rent out apartments. Bad kitchen, and you live with other students who do not clean up after themselves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find other tenants you before hand, because it can be a bit hard to live with other people. But that is also an experience

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit expensive to rent a room in Barcelona, hard to avoid scammers.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to wait 2 hours to sign some papers, but the courses we were enrolled in, at the begenning when we arrived the 13th of september, was not the nescescary the one we ended with. I waited until the 30th of september until I knew my final courses. Not nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not much help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In August I applied for courses, but when I had ti apply for courses I did not get the link, so all the courses I wanted were taken. I was told I could changed when I arrived to Barcelona, but I was only aviable to change it the 30th of september so there was a lot of days without knowing if I could attend to the university because I had to get some specific courses. It ended up with me getting the courses I wanted, but it was a hard and burecratic process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to search for the courselist beforehand, and make an excel file were you try to fit courses so you dont get double booked. It was hard for me to find courses who did not have classes at the same time. Remember to find the correct year, I was looking for 2023-2024 list and I needed the 2024-2025 list so it was a waste of time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice to have some easy courses, but I got a bit tired of other students who did not know have to take the derrivivate of basic functions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Public Sector Economics 3rd year course, is just a combination of Micro I, Micro II and ØPA, on an easier level. 
Macroeconomic IV, 3rd year course, good teacher, Luiz Brotherhood. A bit hard, but he is so good at explaining stuff, and just a nice guy. 
Game Theory for Business, 3rd year course, was quite easy but the solutions to the excercises was not uploaded so you had to be there all the class's
World Economic History, 1st year course, quite easy but 1 out of 2 professors were quite bad. 
International Economics, 3rd year course, bad teacher, tough exam does not have much to do with the things you learn doing the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Was a bit weird that the class were teams of 30-40 people but it was easy to ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Sector Economics 3rd year course
Macroeconomic IV, 3rd year course
Game Theory for Business, 3rd year course
World Economic History, 1st year course
International Economics, 3rd year course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I will probably recommend to take the these courses, because I got them transfered as follows:
Public Sector Economics 3rd year course as Økonomisk Valgfag at KU
Macroeconomic IV, 3rd year course, as Macro III at KU
Game Theory for Business, 3rd year course as Micro III at KU
World Economic History, 1st year course as Økonomisk Historie at KU
International Economics, 3rd year course, at prioriteret økonomisk valg at KU

Maybe take Global Sustainability instead of Public Sector Economics or International Economics. Especially International Economics was a bit harder than I expected because the teahcer were so bad. Or maybe take Corporate Finance instead.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Easy transport(metro-card), get it. Cheap beers, and supermarket as LIDL is around 10-20% cheaper than in copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not use it. So I dont know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some sports and some events, but did no go to them only Erasmus events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to ESN-(Erasmus social Network) activities. This is were I meet new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to monserrat if you want to walk a mountain. Maybe visit Girona and some of the cheaper trips around i catalonia offered by erasmus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not really talk to the local students who had courses with us exchange students, they talked a bit loud in the class. But the few ones I talked to were super nice. I meet one nice student in the gym. But the culture between exchange students is quite nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to ESN events,

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are not good at speaking english in Barcelona. But if you can understand a bit spanish or french it is a bit easier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found it why they also want to be independt, the catalan people. Just by listineng to their language, I found out that it is close to french and spanish, which probalby also is why they want to be independent of Spain.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to ESN-activities to get new friends, ask for exam in December, then you will have free time in all of january. I had my exams the 10th, 18th, 19th and 20th December, so I injoyed the vacation from 20th December 2025 until 9 februar 2025.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find accomodation to apartment by asking university, and prepare you courses 100% before you go to Barcelona.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Taking easy courses, and getting new danish friends. And I had more time to go to the gym because I only needed to pass the courses that was quite nice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably the first day when I lost my luggage and could not enter my apartment. I worked it all out, but at the time it was a bit frusturating.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
